sources.entry: PC Mode - Free app that brings Windows habits to your Mac: delete from Finder with the Delete key, cut and move files with ⌘X and ⌘V, and switch individual windows with ⌘Tab. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/getguruhat/PCMode) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon] ![Native App][Native Icon]

summary.one_liner: PC Mode is a macOS menu-bar utility that brings Windows-style habits to Finder and window switching, such as deleting with a media key, cut-and-move with Cmd+X/Cmd+V, and per-window Cmd+Tab.
summary.what_it_does: PC Mode runs as a menu-bar app and changes several Finder and window-switching behaviors. In Finder, pressing the selected media key (F7 Rewind by default, or F7 to F12 as chosen) moves the selected items to the Trash. Cmd+X marks files as copied, and the next Cmd+V in a destination folder moves them; copying again, changing the clipboard, or leaving Finder cancels the pending move. Cmd+Tab switches between individual windows, including hidden and minimized ones, with Shift+Tab to go backward and Escape to cancel; it can be disabled to restore standard macOS behavior. The switcher also shows each app's CPU and memory use, including helper processes, with CPU highlighted orange at 40% and red at 90%, and RAM highlighted only above 1 GB under memory pressure. Settings open from the menu-bar icon and changes save immediately.
use_cases: delete files from Finder with a key instead of dragging to Trash
cut and paste files between Finder folders
switch between individual windows with Cmd+Tab
bring Windows keyboard habits to a Mac
see which apps use the most CPU or memory while switching
unhide or restore minimized windows quickly
how_to_run: Download PCMode-Installer.dmg from the GitHub Releases page (or the repository link if no release is published).
Open the disk image and drag PC Mode.app to the Applications folder.
Enable PC Mode in System Settings → Privacy & Security → Accessibility and Input Monitoring (use the Settings Manage button to open the requests).
To build from source (macOS 13+, Swift Command Line Tools): run ./test.sh, then ./build-app.sh.
notable: Finder delete mapped to a selectable media key (F7 to F12)
Cmd+X / Cmd+V move semantics for Finder files
Window-level Cmd+Tab that includes hidden and minimized windows
CPU and RAM per app in the switcher, including helper processes, matching Activity Monitor measurements
Ships with a test script covering shortcut, move state, key mapping, and switcher logic
caveats: Requires macOS 13 or later and needs Accessibility and Input Monitoring permissions; the macOS 27 name for the Accessibility setting differs.
Local builds are ad-hoc signed, so rebuilding can require granting permissions again.
Other keyboard remappers should be quit to avoid conflicting shortcuts; some apps may restrict which windows are exposed.
